LanguageData.CBF_S_NewTip: Create a new settlement. It gets town, suburb and countryside.
LanguageData.CBF_S_PickOne: Pick a settlement on the left.
LanguageData.CBF_S_OpenFileTip: Opens the settlement's file in your text editor. The editor reloads changes made there on its own.
LanguageData.CBF_S_FactionOverviewTip: Shows for each faction which settlements it gets and how often.
LanguageData.CBF_S_RerollTip: Recalculates the preview with a new seed.
LanguageData.CBF_S_KindTip: Click switches to the next kind.
LanguageData.CBF_S_ForAll: For all factions of these levels
LanguageData.CBF_S_FactionsTip: Factions or faction categories that explicitly get this settlement.
LanguageData.CBF_S_OwnerAlle: For all factions of these levels
LanguageData.CBF_S_OwnerAlleTip: This plan applies to every faction whose tech level is ticked, unless that faction has plans of its own through faction tags. Its own plans always win.
LanguageData.CBF_S_OwnerFraktionenTip: Only the factions or faction categories listed below get this settlement.
LanguageData.CBF_S_OwnerKeineTip: No faction gets this settlement. Only quests and sites can use it.
LanguageData.CBF_S_OwnerKeineInfo: Only quests and sites can use this settlement.
LanguageData.CBF_S_NoFactionFits: No faction gets this settlement. Pick a tech level with For all factions or add a faction.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MergeTip: Merges the patch files written by the editor into one.
LanguageData.CBF_S_GateWithoutWall: Without a wall there is no gate a gatehouse could fit into. Emplacements still work, the planner puts them on the outline of the town.
LanguageData.CBF_S_UnknownEntry: {0} does not exist. The entry is skipped.
LanguageData.CBF_S_ListGone: The pawn list {0} no longer exists.
LanguageData.CBF_S_FieldNoPlants: A field in {0} has no plants yet.
LanguageData.CBF_S_PenNoAnimals: A pen in {0} has no animals yet.
LanguageData.CBF_S_WeightHint: against other settlements of the same faction
LanguageData.CBF_S_FooterHint: Right-click a tech level to pick it and all higher ones
LanguageData.CBF_S_PreviewWindowTip: Opens the preview large in its own window, with legend and tally.
LanguageData.CBF_S_FarmHousesTip: Which pieces the field is laid around, for example a wind turbine or a mill. Without a choice the planner uses small houses and farmsteads.
LanguageData.CBF_S_CropListTip: Picks a crop list from the Lists tab. The field then draws its plants from it by weight; the individually chosen plants only serve as fallback.
LanguageData.CBF_S_CropListPenTip: Picks a crop list for the pen's growth.
LanguageData.CBF_S_CropListNew: New crop list in the Lists tab
LanguageData.CBF_S_CropListGone: The crop list {0} in {1} does not exist.
LanguageData.CBF_S_GateTip: The door for the passages in this ward's wall. Empty takes the door from the material list. Gatehouses are set under Fortification.
LanguageData.CBF_S_DistrictPlacementTip: Where the district starts. Tick what it should lie near. Several ticks count equally, the district seeks a spot that suits all of them. Nothing ticked: it starts at a random spot away from the other districts.
LanguageData.CBF_S_WdStageTip: World Domination tier 1 to 4 this settlement type stands for. A World Domination settlement of this tier prefers it among the types its faction may get. 0 means no tier.
LanguageData.CBF_S_RiafHoldingTip: Makes this settlement type the plan for villages, towns or garrisons of A Rim of Ice and Fire. CBF then builds the houses and walls of such holdings; defenders, levies, residents and stores stay with A Rim of Ice and Fire. A type with a holding kind is not used for normal settlements.
LanguageData.CBF_Lb_ButtonTip: Loot value of the settlement of this type that was built last.
LanguageData.CBF_Lb_NoneYet: Build a settlement of this type first. Its loot is counted while it is built.
LanguageData.CBF_Lb_Note: Market value of everything lying around or stored in containers. Medieval Overhaul lootables that fill only when searched are not included.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MaterialListTip: The material list decides which walls, floors, doors and other things the pieces of this settlement type get.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MaterialListNone: No material list chosen. Without one this settlement type is switched off.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MaterialListUnusable: This material list is unusable, critical roles find no thing.
LanguageData.CBF_S_WdTypeTip: World Domination settlement types this plan stands for, such as mining camp or slave village. Only types of the chosen tier are offered. Empty means any type.
LanguageData.CBF_S_AddWardTip: Add a ward this settlement type does not have yet.
LanguageData.CBF_S_NoWdLootTip: Switches off the extra loot World Domination 2.0 adds to settlements of this type.
LanguageData.CBF_S_IdeoStyleTip: Furniture gets the style of the owning faction's ideoligion.
LanguageData.CBF_S_CampKindsTip: Quest sites this camp plan builds, for example bandit camps, outposts or work sites. Only used for settlements of the kind camp.
LanguageData.CBF_S_IdeoEntryTip: Ideoligion condition: this entry is only built when the faction's ideoligion has, or lacks, the chosen memes or precepts.
LanguageData.CBF_PreviewWardsTip: Colours the old town, suburb and countryside in the preview.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MineTip: A mine dug into the rock from a building of this district: a tunnel with chambers.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MineOreShareTip: Share of rock cells along the mine that become ore, from 0 to 1.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MineHutsTip: Categories of the buildings the mine may start from. Empty: any building of the district.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MineThingsTip: Things in the mine. Click to open the window where you enter them by place.
LanguageData.CBF_S_TreeShareTip: Share of the wild trees inside the settlement that stay standing when it is built, from 0 to 1. 0 clears them all.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MapSizeTip: Edge length of the map this settlement type asks for, 150 to 400. The larger of this and the world setting is used.
LanguageData.CBF_S_CoreSizeTip: Edge length of the settlement core in cells, as a range. The suburb and the countryside grow around it.
LanguageData.CBF_S_LocCenterTip: The district starts as close to the middle of its ward as possible.
LanguageData.CBF_S_LocGateTip: The district starts close to a gate.
LanguageData.CBF_S_LocWallTip: The district starts close to the wall of its ward.
LanguageData.CBF_S_LocMainTip: The district starts along the main road.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MinePlace_EntranceTip: On the first cells of the tunnel, right behind the mine entrance at the hut.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MinePlace_TunnelTip: Along the tunnels, only where the tunnel is wide enough to pass by.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MinePlace_ChamberTip: In a chamber at the end of a tunnel. Small things stand by the wall.
LanguageData.CBF_MineWin_StuffTip: Material of the thing. Empty takes stone or wood of the map.
LanguageData.CBF_MineWin_ContentTip: Goods laid onto the thing, for example iron on a shelf or in a crate. What does not fit is left out.
LanguageData.CBF_MineWin_MoveTip: Move to another place in the mine.
LanguageData.CBF_S_RangeOutside: A value is outside the allowed range of {0} to {1}.
LanguageData.CBF_S_RangeOrder: The minimum is larger than the maximum.
LanguageData.CBF_D_AddLevelTip: Adds a level below the lowest one.
LanguageData.CBF_D_LastLevel: A dungeon needs at least one level.
LanguageData.CBF_D_DeleteLevelAsk: Remove level {0}? Its areas hold {1} entries.
LanguageData.CBF_D_OnSurface: in the mountain of the surface map
LanguageData.CBF_D_EntranceNone: Empty means the generator opens a plain tunnel into the mountain.
LanguageData.CBF_D_StairsUpHint: The stairs up are placed where the stairs down of the level above stand.
LanguageData.CBF_D_LowestHint: This is the lowest level. It needs no stairs down.
LanguageData.CBF_D_DecoTip: Placed on the corridor floor against the wall, on both sides at random. Wall fixtures such as torches face the wall, everything else faces into the corridor. Edge and Road make no difference here.
LanguageData.CBF_D_SectionDecoInherit: Empty means the level's corridor decor applies here.
LanguageData.CBF_D_CorridorsNone: Empty means plain corridor cells. Corners, junctions and ends are built by the generator.
LanguageData.CBF_D_AreasTip: Which areas this level can have, each with its buildings, like the districts of a ward.
LanguageData.CBF_D_CountUnit: times, each copy is a level of its own
LanguageData.CBF_D_CountTip: Builds this level several times in a row, 1 to 20. Each copy is generated anew. The spread counts every copy as a level.
LanguageData.CBF_D_SectionsTip: Splits the level into sections in a row. The first section holds the entrance, the last one the stairs down. Each section has its own areas and can have its own corridor segments.
LanguageData.CBF_D_SectionsNone: No sections. The whole level is one section with the areas below.
LanguageData.CBF_D_AddSectionFirstTip: The first section takes over the areas of the level.
LanguageData.CBF_D_DeleteSectionAsk: Remove section {0}? Its areas hold {1} entries.
LanguageData.CBF_D_SectionUpTip: Move this section one towards the entrance.
LanguageData.CBF_D_SectionDownTip: Move this section one towards the stairs down.
LanguageData.CBF_D_SectionCorridorsInherit: None set: the section uses the corridor segments of the level.
LanguageData.CBF_S_PriorityTip: Which entry gets space first. With equal priority the previous order applies (minimum count, size). Low entries may stay below their minimum when space runs out.
LanguageData.CBF_Pr_ButtonTip: Plans this settlement type many times on different terrain and shows how often it works and what gets left out.
LanguageData.CBF_Pr_Ask: The check plans this settlement {0} times on flat land, rivers, mountains, coast and the worst case. This can take one to a few minutes. Start?
LanguageData.CBF_Pr_Stopped: Cancelled after {0} of {1} runs. The result only covers these runs.
LanguageData.CBF_Pr_Verdict_Gelb: The plan often works, but fails on some terrain. Lower minimum counts or set less important entries to Low.
LanguageData.CBF_Pr_Verdict_Rot: The plan fails too often. It asks for more than fits. Lower minimum counts, remove entries or allow a larger map.
LanguageData.CBF_Pr_Means: On average {0} attempts and {1} s per run.
LanguageData.CBF_Pr_EstimateLine: The minimum counts need {0} cells of edge length, up to the maximum counts {3}. {1} are possible (map size {2}).
LanguageData.CBF_Pr_EstimateNote: The estimate is a rough guess without planning. The runs above are what counts.
LanguageData.CBF_Pr_OmittedNone: Every entry reached its minimum in every run.
LanguageData.CBF_Pr_OmittedLine: {0}: below its minimum of {3} in {1} of {2} runs
LanguageData.CBF_Pr_OmittedHint: Red: left out in at least half of the runs. Lower its minimum, set it to Low or move it to a ward with more room.
LanguageData.CBF_Pr_Space: Space: the minimum counts need {0} of {1} cells of edge length ({2} %), up to the maximum counts {4} (map size {3})
LanguageData.CBF_Pr_SpaceTip: Quick estimate without planning. Red means even the minimum counts do not fit, yellow that they are tight or the maximum counts do not fully fit. It updates with every change. Check plan gives the reliable answer.
LanguageData.CBF_Pr_SpaceDo_Gelb: Tight. On rough terrain some entries may be left out. Check plan shows which.
LanguageData.CBF_Pr_SpaceDo_Rot: Probably too big. Lower minimum counts, set entries to Low or allow a larger map, then use Check plan.
LanguageData.CBF_S_SuburbRingTip: Only for a suburb wall with a walkway (depth 3 or more). On: the suburb becomes a closed ring around the town. Off: the suburb stays as separate areas on the sides, as many as Suburb areas allows. With Suburb areas at 0 the ring stays.
LanguageData.CBF_S_SuburbOnlyTip: These fields only apply to settlement types with a suburb ward. Add a suburb ward under Wards to use them.
LanguageData.CBF_Pr_Stopping: Cancelling. The current run finishes its step first.
LanguageData.CBF_Pr_StuckHint: The run does not react. You can close the window anyway; the run then ends in the background.
LanguageData.CBF_Pr_NoDungeon: Not available for dungeons. Use Preview for them.
LanguageData.CBF_D_SectionFirst: This is already the first section.
LanguageData.CBF_D_SectionLast: This is already the last section.
LanguageData.CBF_D_OrphanAreas: The level still has {0} area(s) of its own. With sections they do not apply.
LanguageData.CBF_D_OrphanAreasTake: Move them into the first section
LanguageData.CBF_D_SpreadNone: Nothing yet. Entries here are placed on any level within their range, in addition to the areas.
LanguageData.CBF_D_SpreadDistrictGone: {0} should go into area {1}, but no level has that area.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_caveWidth: Width of the cave passages between the areas, 1 to 5 cells. Each passage picks a width within the range.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_caveShare: Share of the connections that become natural caves instead of built corridors.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_secretChance: Chance that a room door, which would otherwise be bricked up, gets a narrow secret passage through the rock to the nearest corridor or to the door of another room. The door becomes a secret door (material list role DOOR_SECRET). At most this share of the rooms gets one.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_levelMapSize: Size of the map of this level. 0 takes the size from the layout. Ignored on the first level, it lies on the surface map.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_spread: Buildings the generator spreads over several levels: a total count over a range of levels.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SpreadEntry_levels: From which to which level, counted from the top. Level 1 lies in the mountain of the surface map.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_SpreadEntry_district: Area the buildings go into. "any" lets the generator choose.
LanguageData.CBF_D_Layout_CorridorsTip: A main corridor network, the rooms dock onto it.
LanguageData.CBF_D_Layout_ChambersTip: Rooms sit directly against each other, without corridors in between.
LanguageData.CBF_D_Layout_GridTip: Rooms on a loose grid with thick rock between them, joined by short straight passages and many loops.
LanguageData.CBF_D_Layout_TempleTip: A large central hall with wings laid out in pairs along its axes, side chambers and a winding cave passage.
LanguageData.CBF_D_Layout_WarrenTip: Rooms grow against each other, share their walls and open into each other through doors in the wall.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_layout: How the level is built. Corridors: a main corridor network with rooms docked onto it. Chambers: rooms directly against each other. Rows: a main corridor with bends, rooms in rows along both sides. Grid: rooms on a loose grid with short passages and many loops. Temple: a central hall with paired wings. Warren: rooms sharing their walls.
LanguageData.CBF_D_Layout_CaveTip: Natural cave chambers without built walls.
LanguageData.CBF_D_Layout_RowsTip: A main corridor with a few bends. The rooms stand in rows along both sides and share their walls, the largest room closes off the end. Now and then a wall with a door cuts the corridor.
LanguageData.CBF_FieldDesc_DistrictSpec_layout: Own layout for this area. Empty takes the layout of the level.
LanguageData.CBF_S_MountainMantleTip: Minimum rock thickness around old town and suburb, 0 to {0}. A mountain city uses {1} when this is 0. Other types only get a mountain when this is set.
LanguageData.CBF_S_DarkPlants: Fields inside the mountain are dark. These plants do not grow there: {0}. Choose plants that grow in the dark, such as mushrooms.
LanguageData.CBF_S_WeightFromCategory: Category entries have no weight of their own here. The pieces of the category are drawn by their own weights.
LanguageData.CBF_S_PlanRuinTip: Builds every place of this type as a ruin: walls torn down, rooms burnt out, roofs partly collapsed, overgrown. The faction still lives there. Plundered means little loot, not plundered means the loot stays. A ruin from a quest or site takes precedence.
LanguageData.CBF_S_PlanWhereTip: Conditions for this settlement type. Empty rows restrict nothing.
LanguageData.CBF_S_RequiresUnknown: Unknown name: {0}. This condition is never met.
LanguageData.CBF_S_RequiresCycle: Cycle: these entries need each other and are never built.
LanguageData.CBF_S_RequiresTip: Condition: this entry is only built if enough of the chosen pieces or categories stand in the whole settlement. Each name counts once. Conditional entries are planned after the others. If the condition is not met, the entry is dropped, even with priority Critical. Dungeons have no conditions.
LanguageData.CBF_S_RequiresCountWrong: The count {0} does not fit {1} chosen names. It must be between 1 and {1}.
LanguageData.CBF_S_PlanIdeoNoDlc: Needs Ideology. Without the DLC this condition is ignored.
LanguageData.CBF_S_PlanIdeoWithTip: Only factions whose main ideoligion has at least one of these memes or precepts get this settlement type. Example: tunneler for a mountain city. Empty means all factions.
LanguageData.CBF_S_PlanIdeoWithoutTip: Factions whose main ideoligion has one of these memes or precepts never get this settlement type. Empty means no restriction.
LanguageData.CBF_S_PlanBiomesTip: The settlement type only appears on tiles of these biomes, for example only in deserts. Empty means all biomes.
LanguageData.CBF_S_PlanNotBiomesTip: The settlement type never appears on tiles of these biomes.
LanguageData.CBF_S_PlanHillinessTip: How hilly the tile is on the world map: flat, small hills, large hills or mountainous. The settlement type only appears at the chosen levels. Empty means all.
LanguageData.CBF_S_PlanLandformsTip: Features of the tile such as coast, river, lake, valley or canyon. The settlement type only appears if the tile has at least one of them. Empty means any.
LanguageData.CBF_S_PlanNotLandformsTip: The settlement type never appears on tiles with one of these landforms.
LanguageData.CBF_S_PlanLoosen: The type only appears where all conditions apply. Without the Ideology DLC, ideoligion conditions are ignored.
LanguageData.CBF_S_TabBasicsTip: What the place looks like: name, kind, material list, sizes, suburb, ruin, map icon.
LanguageData.CBF_S_TabPlacementTip: Who gets the place and where it appears: tech levels, factions, weight and conditions.
LanguageData.CBF_S_TabGarrisonTip: How many defenders the place has: minimum points, wealth factor and share per ward.
LanguageData.CBF_S_TabModsTip: Required mods, takeover, World Domination, A Rim of Ice and Fire and camp types.
LanguageData.CBF_S_GarrisonMinPointsTip: The place always spends at least this many points on defenders, however poor the colony is.
LanguageData.CBF_S_GarrisonFactorTip: Factor on your colony's raid points, the points the storyteller would spend on a raid right now. The place buys its defenders with them, but never for less than the minimum points. Decimals are allowed, such as 0.5 for a village or 1.5 for a large city. Applies when you enter the map.
LanguageData.CBF_S_GarrisonOff: Garrison factor 0: garrison entries are fixed counts as before.
LanguageData.CBF_S_GarrisonAnchors: Pawn anchors count against the budget
LanguageData.CBF_S_GarrisonAnchorsTip: How much of the points of pawns from pawn anchors in the pieces is taken from the budget. At 100 % every anchored pawn replaces a bought one, at 0 % anchored pawns come on top.
LanguageData.CBF_S_GarrisonShareTip: How the bought defenders are spread over the wards. The last ward always gets the rest up to 100%. Raising a ward takes from the last ward first, then from the others from the top.
LanguageData.CBF_S_GarrisonShareAutoTip: Untick to set the shares yourself.
LanguageData.CBF_S_GarrisonEntriesHint: Set fixed pawns in the garrison entries of the wards: tick active, then min, max and weight.
LanguageData.CBF_GarrisonActiveTip: Only active entries load pawns from their list. Min comes first, then extras up to max by weight while the budget lasts. They count against the budget.
LanguageData.CBF_GarrisonWeightTip: Weight: how likely this entry gets extras up to max.
LanguageData.CBF_GarrisonPointsHint: This settlement type uses points. Only active entries place fixed pawns; the rest comes from the faction's settlement group.
LanguageData.CBF_S_GarrisonShareRest: The last ward gets the rest up to 100%.
LanguageData.CBF_GP_Budget: Minimum points {0}, raid points {1} × factor {2} × garrison size {3} = {4}, budget {5} (the higher value)
LanguageData.CBF_GP_NoPoints: Without point system: minimum points {0} × garrison size {1}
LanguageData.CBF_GP_NoFaction: No faction: {0} points per pawn assumed.
LanguageData.CBF_GP_NoGroupMaker: The faction has no pawn group maker: {0} points per pawn assumed.
LanguageData.CBF_GP_NoLayout: No layout: pawn anchors not counted.
LanguageData.CBF_GP_Capped: Limit of {0} pawns per settlement reached.
LanguageData.CBF_GR_OpenTip: Shows how many defenders this settlement type fields for a faction and a number of raid points, per ward.
LanguageData.CBF_GR_FactionTip: The faction decides which pawns are bought from its settlement group and what they cost.
LanguageData.CBF_GR_Layout: Plan the layout so pawn anchors count
LanguageData.CBF_GR_LayoutTip: Plans the place once without a map, like the preview, and counts the pawn anchors of the placed pieces. Without a layout anchors do not count.
LanguageData.CBF_GR_Sum: Total {0} pawns: {1} visible, {2} in reserve, combat power {3}
LanguageData.CBF_GR_ColShareTip: Share of the bought pawns this ward gets.
LanguageData.CBF_GR_ColFixedTip: Pawns from active garrison entries, as expected value.
LanguageData.CBF_GR_ColAnchorsTip: Pawns from pawn anchors in pieces. Only with a layout.
LanguageData.CBF_GR_ColPointsTip: Pawns the faction buys with the budget.
LanguageData.CBF_GR_ColVisibleTip: Pawns standing on the map at once.
LanguageData.CBF_GR_ColPowerTip: Sum of the pawns' combat power.
LanguageData.CBF_GP_OverBudget: Warning: fixed pawns and anchors cost {0} points and exceed the budget of {1}. With these settings there is no mobile garrison from points.
LanguageData.CBF_S_GarrisonShareTipDungeon: How the bought defenders of the whole dungeon are spread over its levels. The budget is set once when the first level is entered. The last level always gets the rest up to 100%. Raising a level takes from the last level first, then from the others from the top. A level repeated ×n gets its share once per repetition; the shares are then scaled to 100%.
LanguageData.CBF_S_GarrisonShareAutoDungeon: Share automatically, rising towards the bottom
LanguageData.CBF_S_GarrisonShareAutoTipDungeon: Ticked, deeper levels get more defenders, the deepest the most. Untick to set the shares yourself.
LanguageData.CBF_S_GarrisonEntriesHintDungeon: Set fixed pawns in the garrison entries of the levels: tick active, then min, max and weight.
LanguageData.CBF_S_GarrisonShareRestDungeon: The last level gets the rest up to 100%.
LanguageData.CBF_GR_ColLevelTip: Level of the dungeon, counted from the top.
LanguageData.CBF_GR_LayoutDungeon: Pawn anchors of dungeons are not counted here
LanguageData.CBF_GR_LayoutDungeonTip: Dungeon levels are planned only when they are entered. The calculator shows the dungeon without its pawn anchors.
LanguageData.CBF_GR_AnchorsLayout: Counted on the planned layout (≈). A settlement varies by a few pawns from map to map, the game can field somewhat more.
LanguageData.CBF_GR_AnchorsEstimated: Pawns from anchors are a rough estimate from the districts and only a lower bound (≥). The layout is being planned for a closer count.
LanguageData.CBF_GR_SmallVaries: Small places such as villages vary a lot in the game, by about a quarter up or down from map to map.
LanguageData.CBF_S_DecoSketchTip: Sketch of a stretch of road with the entries below in their colours. Spacing and max are shown roughly.
LanguageData.CBF_S_DecoSketchEmpty: No street decor yet. Add a template below.
LanguageData.CBF_S_DecoPlaceTip: Edge: beside the road. Road: on the road itself.
LanguageData.CBF_S_DecoWhatTip: A piece, a piece category or an object list. Single things go into an object list.
LanguageData.CBF_S_DecoSpacingTip: Cells between two placements, as a range. Smaller means denser.
LanguageData.CBF_S_DecoMaxTip: At most this many per ward. 0 means no limit.
LanguageData.CBF_S_WeightShortTip: Weight against the other entries of this ward.
LanguageData.CBF_S_DecoT_LightTip: Adds a street light entry at the edge with matching spacing, then lets you pick or create the object list.
LanguageData.CBF_S_DecoT_SideTip: Adds an entry for benches, barrels and crates at the edge, then lets you pick or create the object list.
LanguageData.CBF_S_DecoT_SignTip: Adds a sign entry at the edge with wide spacing, then lets you pick or create the object list.
LanguageData.CBF_S_DecoT_RoadTip: Adds an entry on the road, at most 3, then lets you pick or create the object list.
LanguageData.CBF_S_DecoT_PieceTip: Adds an entry for small street pieces, at most 2, then lets you pick a piece or category.
LanguageData.CBF_S_DecoOwnTip: Pick a piece, a category or an object list yourself.
LanguageData.CBF_S_DecoEditList: Open the object list and see or change what it places.
LanguageData.CBF_D_LayoutsTip: Tick one or more layouts. With several, each generated level rolls one of them.
LanguageData.CBF_D_LayoutsRandom: Each generated level rolls one of the ticked layouts.
LanguageData.CBF_D_CorridorStripTip: The corridor as it is built: the segments in their order, with the corridor decor on top. A section without decor of its own shows the decor of the level.
LanguageData.CBF_D_SectionRolesTip: Entrance: the way in lies in this section. On the first level that is the entrance from the surface, on lower levels the stairs up.\nStairs down: the stairs to the next level are built in this section.\nThe first section always holds the entrance, the last one the stairs down. The arrows change the order.
